name: accumulator
description: Ground truth for tools/hal_explain/fixtures/accumulator.v. Blocks are matched by their gate set, never by block_id, so the reference stays valid if the numbering scheme changes. The confidences are the ones the recorded findings documents in this directory imply; changing a status in one of those documents must change this file too.

blocks.note: DANA groups the four accumulator flip-flops. It is a structural guess and the block must stay 'heuristic' even though a verified adder claims the same flip-flops.
module_identification builds candidates around known registers, so the verified cone contains the accumulator flip-flops as well; that is the deliberate overlap with the DANA group.

DANA's group and hal_fsm's machine have the same gate set, so they compose into ONE block that carries both strengths: two heuristic claims (the two candidate proposals) and two verified ones (the transition relation and the reachable set).
checked by module_identification and not verified. It must render as inconclusive, never as 'no function here'.

unknown_regions.note: a tie cell, reachable only through a constant net, so it clusters with nothing

the controller's next-state logic. hal_fsm scopes its findings to the state register only and never names the transition logic it handed to solve_fsm, so these five gates are genuinely unclaimed by every document in this model. See tools/hal_explain/README.md, 'Integration notes'.

notes: gates_heuristic is 0 on purpose: every gate the DANA group covers is also covered by the verified adder, so no gate's strongest claim is a heuristic. The register block itself stays heuristic.
gates_unknown_confidence is 3: the parity cone, whose only claim is inconclusive.
